cards.explanation: The answer is silent. The LORD says, “Be silent before Me, O islands…” (Isaiah 41:1). Think of a room going quiet right before somebody important starts to talk, friends. Nobody plans that hush. It just happens.

The answer is True. The one from the east is not stuck standing around. The LORD says, “He hands nations over to him and subdues kings before him.” (Isaiah 41:2). He's moving, and the kings are the ones getting handled.

The answer is False. The text says, “He pursues them, going on safely, hardly touching the path with his feet.” (Isaiah 41:3). He's the one doing the chasing, and nothing there says he's dragging or struggling. Feet that hardly touch the path and a man going on safely sound like someone moving with ease.

The answer is the LORD Himself. He asks who performed all this and carried it out, then answers it in His own voice with “…I am He.” (Isaiah 41:4). Calling forth the generations from the beginning is His work. Nobody else steps up to the microphone.
The answer is fear. The text says, “The islands see and fear; the ends of the earth tremble.” (Isaiah 41:5). The islands see, and fear is what comes next. They also approach and come forward.

The answer is Be strong. “Each one helps the other and says to his brother, ‘Be strong!’” (Isaiah 41:6). It's people lifting each other up while the ends of the earth tremble. Everybody needs a friend like that in the moment, friends.

The answer is nail it down. “He nails it down so it will not be toppled.” (Isaiah 41:7). Just before that, the one who wields the hammer cheers on the one who strikes the anvil, saying of the welding, “It is good.” When I really want my cookie boxes to stay shut, I'm not shy with the tape either.
The answer is My friend. The LORD says, “…Abraham My friend…” (Isaiah 41:8). Abraham was Israel's ancestor, and that's the name the LORD gives him here. I'd take that title over any trophy, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “You are My servant.” Then He adds, “I have chosen and not rejected you.” (Isaiah 41:9). His choosing and His not rejecting go together. That's good news you can build a day on.

The answer is that He is with them. “Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God.” (Isaiah 41:10). The reason isn't a plan or a number. It's the LORD being right there with them.

The answer is strengthen, and the verse says it first. The LORD says, “I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.” (Isaiah 41:10). Strength, help and upholding all come in one breath, friends. Hard to ask for a better promise.

The answer is that they will be ashamed and disgraced. “Behold, all who rage against you will be ashamed and disgraced; those who contend with you will be reduced to nothing and will perish.” (Isaiah 41:11). The ones raging against Israel don't come out on top. It's the LORD's promise to His people.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “You will seek them but will not find them.” (Isaiah 41:12). Israel looks for those who waged war against them, and there's nothing left to find. Those enemies come to nothing.

The answer is the Holy One of Israel. The LORD says, “Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.” (Isaiah 41:14). Right before that He says, “Do not fear, O Jacob, you worm, O few men of Israel.” Then He names who stands behind them, and that name is worth remembering, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD says, “…I will make you into a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth.” (Isaiah 41:15). Nothing worn out about it. A sledge like that can thresh mountains.

The answer is rejoice in the LORD. “But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.” (Isaiah 41:16). The wind carries the chaff off, and Israel's joy goes to the LORD. The glory goes to Him too.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.” (Isaiah 41:17). The poor and needy are parched, and He promises not to forsake them. That's a promise worth holding onto, friends.

The answer is desert. The LORD says, “I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into flowing springs.” (Isaiah 41:18). A desert becomes a pool of water. The dry land gets flowing springs too, and that's quite a change.

The answer is so all will know the LORD did it. The LORD says it's “…so that all may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this and the Holy One of Israel has created it.” (Isaiah 41:20). Every river and every tree points back to Him, friends. He wants everyone to see whose hand did it.
